name: Concierge
description: Natural-language search for your Jellyfin library — describe a film and find it, including by the lines spoken in it.
overview: Search your library the way you'd describe a film to a friend.

versions.changelog: The current build. Search survives a model that fails: a fallback profile is tried before giving up, and a rejected, unreachable, unreadable or unanswering model no longer silently costs the pass you paid for. Everything below, plus a settings page where what you save is what runs.

The build where OpenAI-compatible endpoints became usable. Servers that answer with nulls where OpenAI sends objects no longer crash the parser, and a reply that stops mid-sentence keeps the rankings it finished instead of discarding all of them. Stop here if you want the compatible provider path without the fallback model above.

The last build of the interface era, before the work turned to providers and robustness. The search-box toggle turns Concierge off rather than rearranging it, the settings page is wide enough for the Models table, episodes can run on their own model, and the Library tab shows episodes under their show. Stop here if you want the finished interface on a single, well-behaved provider.

The build where the search box started working again. A stray brace had killed the injected client script from 0.18.0.0 through 0.22.0.0 — five releases where typing in Jellyfin's search box did nothing at all, while the settings page kept working and hid it. This is the first release after that, and the oldest one worth installing.

The build where results became instant. The free keyword answer paints in about a millisecond and the ranked one replaces it when it lands, so nothing waits on a model to show something real. Posters render, and turning thinking off finally took effect on OpenAI. Note the search-box script is broken from 0.18.0.0 to 0.22.0.0 — this is the last good build before that window.

The build where results first reached the Jellyfin search box as poster cards, above the request rows. Also the fix for an upgrade that silently did nothing: the client script URL never changed between releases and carried no cache headers, so browsers kept running the old one.

Everything before the search box. Natural-language search over your library from the plugin's own page: hybrid keyword and semantic retrieval, an enrichment pass that writes what each item is about, a plan pass that reads constraints out of a sentence, quote search over your own subtitles and lyrics, checkpointing so a cancelled index build loses nothing, and an append-only query log with per-call costs.
